title: Forces and momentum
summary: Newton’s three laws, free-body diagrams, friction and drag, linear momentum and impulse, collisions and explosions, and the force needed for circular motion.

keyterms.definition: An object stays at rest or moves with constant velocity unless a resultant external force acts on it.
The resultant force equals the rate of change of momentum, F = Δp/Δt; for constant mass, F = ma.
If body A exerts a force on body B, B exerts an equal and opposite force of the same type on A.
A diagram of one object showing every external force on it as an arrow from its point of application.
The state in which the resultant force on an object is zero, so its velocity is constant.
A contact force opposing relative sliding of surfaces; static friction ≤ μ_s F_N, dynamic friction = μ_d F_N.
Product of mass and velocity, p = mv; a vector measured in kg m s⁻¹ (or N s).
Change in momentum produced by a force, J = FΔt; equal to the area under a force–time graph.
The total momentum of a system is constant if no resultant external force acts on it.
A collision in which total kinetic energy is conserved as well as momentum.
The resultant force towards the centre needed for circular motion, F = mv²/r = mω²r.
Rate of change of angle, ω = 2π/T; for circular motion v = ωr.

questions.prompt: A book rests on a table. According to Newton’s third law, what is the partner of the book’s weight?
options: The normal force from the table on the book
The friction force on the book
The gravitational pull of the book on the Earth
The book’s push on the table
questions.explanation: Third-law pairs act on different bodies and are the same type of force: Earth pulls the book gravitationally, so the book pulls Earth gravitationally.

questions.statement: An object moving at constant velocity must have no forces acting on it.
questions.explanation: Constant velocity requires zero RESULTANT force; several forces may act but balance.

questions.text: A resultant force of 12 N acts on a 3.0 kg trolley. Its acceleration is ___ m s⁻².

questions.prompt: A 60 kg person stands in a lift accelerating upwards at 2.0 m s⁻² (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). What is the normal force from the floor?
Match each force to its description.

pairs.right: Pull along a string or cable
Resistance from a fluid opposing motion

questions.explanation: Each force on a free-body diagram has a specific cause and direction.

questions.prompt: A box is pushed with 50 N across a floor at constant velocity. What is the friction force on the box?
questions.explanation: Constant velocity means equilibrium, so friction exactly balances the 50 N push.

questions.statement: The coefficient of static friction is usually greater than or equal to the coefficient of dynamic friction.
questions.explanation: It typically takes more force to start an object sliding than to keep it sliding.

questions.text: A 5.0 kg block rests on a level floor with μ_s = 0.40 (g = 9.8 m s⁻²). The largest horizontal force it can take without sliding is ___ N.
questions.explanation: Maximum static friction = μ_s F_N = 0.40 × 5.0 × 9.8 = 19.6 N.

questions.prompt: Which free-body diagram feature shows that a parachutist is falling at terminal velocity?
options: The weight and drag arrows are equal in length
The drag arrow is longer than the weight arrow
The arrows point the same way
questions.explanation: At terminal velocity the resultant force is zero, so drag and weight are equal and opposite.

questions.prompt: Order the steps for solving a Newton’s second law problem.
items: Isolate the object and draw its free-body diagram
Apply F = ma to find the unknown
questions.explanation: A clear free-body diagram and sign convention prevent the most common errors.

questions.prompt: A 0.15 kg ball moving at 20 m s⁻¹ is caught and stopped. What impulse does the hand exert on it?
options: 3.0 N s opposite to its motion
3.0 N s in its direction of motion
questions.explanation: J = Δp = 0 − 0.15 × 20 = −3.0 N s: magnitude 3.0 N s, opposite to the motion.

questions.statement: Airbags reduce injury by reducing the change in momentum of the passenger.
questions.explanation: The momentum change is the same; the airbag increases the stopping time, so the average force F = Δp/Δt is smaller.

questions.text: The area under a force–time graph equals the ___.
questions.explanation: Impulse = ∫F dt = change in momentum.

questions.prompt: A 2.0 kg trolley at 3.0 m s⁻¹ hits a stationary 1.0 kg trolley and they stick together. What is their common velocity?
questions.explanation: Momentum before = 6.0 kg m s⁻¹ = 3.0 kg × v, so v = 2.0 m s⁻¹.

questions.prompt: In the collision of the previous type (trolleys sticking together), kinetic energy is
options: decreased, so the collision is inelastic
questions.explanation: Before: ½(2)(3²) = 9 J. After: ½(3)(2²) = 6 J. KE is lost to internal energy and sound, so it is inelastic.

questions.statement: In an explosion of an object initially at rest, the total momentum afterwards is zero.
questions.explanation: With no external force, momentum is conserved; the fragments move off with momenta that sum to zero, while kinetic energy increases.

questions.text: A 50 kg skater at rest pushes off a 75 kg skater, who moves at 2.0 m s⁻¹. The 50 kg skater moves off at ___ m s⁻¹.
questions.explanation: 0 = 75 × 2.0 − 50v, so v = 150/50 = 3.0 m s⁻¹ in the opposite direction.

questions.prompt: Match each interaction to what is conserved.
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved whenever there is no external force; kinetic energy is conserved only in elastic collisions.

questions.prompt: A rocket expels 4.0 kg of gas each second at 2500 m s⁻¹ relative to the rocket. What is the thrust?
Order the steps to solve a one-dimensional collision problem.
items: Write total momentum before the collision
Write total momentum after in terms of the unknown
Equate and solve, giving the direction
questions.explanation: Signs matter: velocities in the negative direction carry negative momentum.

questions.prompt: An object moves in a circle at constant speed. Which statement is correct?
options: It is accelerating towards the centre
The resultant force on it is zero
questions.explanation: The direction of velocity keeps changing, so there is a centripetal acceleration v²/r towards the centre.

questions.text: A wheel turns once every 0.50 s. Its angular velocity is ___ rad s⁻¹ (to 3 s.f.).

questions.statement: Centripetal force is an extra force that must be added to a free-body diagram.
questions.explanation: It is not a new force: it is the name for the resultant towards the centre, provided by tension, friction, gravity, etc.

questions.prompt: A 0.20 kg ball on a string moves in a horizontal circle of radius 0.50 m at 3.0 m s⁻¹. What is the centripetal force?
Match each motion to the force providing the centripetal force.

pairs.left: Car turning on a flat road

questions.explanation: Identify the real force that provides the centripetal resultant in each case.

questions.prompt: If the speed of an object in a circle of fixed radius doubles, the centripetal force needed
questions.explanation: F = mv²/r, so F ∝ v²: doubling v multiplies F by 4.

questions.statement: If the string breaks, a ball in horizontal circular motion flies off along the tangent.
questions.explanation: With no centripetal force it continues in a straight line in the direction of its velocity at that instant (Newton’s first law).

questions.text: For an object moving in a circle of radius r with angular velocity ω, its linear speed is v = ___.
questions.explanation: Each radian of rotation moves the object an arc length r, so v = ωr.

questions.prompt: At the top of a vertical loop, a roller-coaster car just keeps contact with the track. Which provides the centripetal force there?
options: Weight plus a large normal force
questions.explanation: At the minimum speed the normal force falls to zero, so mg = mv²/r and v = √(gr).

questions.prompt: A satellite moves in a circular orbit at constant speed. How much work does gravity do on it per orbit?
questions.explanation: The force is always perpendicular to the velocity, so no work is done and the kinetic energy is constant.
